text:
maria: Heads-up — after the 2.1.8 rollout I'm seeing a consistent 12-18% tail-latency bump on host ingress. Traces point at extra slowpath time in the parse/fragmentation layer. anyone seen this?
devon: saw a few spikes in canary earlier, didn’t dig in. is it tokenization or framing?
maria: initial flame shows parse slice + fragment coalesce taking longer. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~6% for short chat requests.
kevin: hmm could be the new kernel selector fallback that landed yesterday. it swaps to the conservative vector path on certain seq-len distributions.
sara: @kevin which CL? I can revert if it's the culprit.
kevin: CL 5402 — added safety when preferred kernel reports OOM-like metrics. thought it only affects long sequences.
maria: logs show lots of tiny fragments (~128–512b) now being routed to slowpath that used to be fastpath. host-side overhead from extra loop + memcopy is visible.
perf-bot: perf summary for 2765432100: ingress_parse_cpu +14%, writev syscalls +22%, avg_kvcache_latency +9ms for hits.
devon: can you paste the stack sample around the slowpath?
maria: here — sample taken at peak:
```
parse_fragment_coalesce()
  -> fragment_router_slowpath()
    -> token_bundle_unmarshal()
      -> kvcache_lookup_miss_handler()
        -> memcpy()
```
kevin: KV miss inside tokenization?? that suggests we are re-parsing prefixes instead of using prefix/KV cache. maybe the slowpath invalidates prefix keys due to a header normalization change.
sara: i remember a normalization tweak in CL 5387 (http2 header canon). could interact.
buildbot: deploy 2.1.8 -> prod at 02:13 UTC yesterday. rollback window closed.
devon: quick repro: send 10k short chats with varied punctuation, look for increased small-frame count and successive KV churn. i can run a canary today.
maria: repro script attached in thread (ran locally). pattern: when fragments are reassembled out-of-order we hit slowpath and then the KV cache sees different keys so hit-rate drops.
kevin: suspect path: new kernel selector marks a frame as 'complex' when headers contain non-ascii quoting; that hits slowpath and changes parsing flow, which changes prefix canonicalization -> kvkey mismatch.
sara: options: 1) revert kernel selector change; 2) make canonicalization deterministic pre-selector; 3) teach KV cache to normalize alternate keys.
devon: for short-term canary I'd prefer 1) or 2). revert is fastest.
maria: agree. also we should add a micro-benchmark: repeated small-fragment scenarios measuring kv hit-rate + parse CPU. want a before/after.
perf-bot: added perf test template "small-frag-kv-hit" to CI.
kevin: i'll put up a revert PR for CL 5402 and add a test that asserts no >5% regression on ingress tail.
sara: i'll coordinate rollback plan with infra and update runbook. add notes to incident channel if rollback starts.
maria: thanks. postmortem follow-ups: (a) add unit test for header normalization idempotence; (b) extend KV cache to accept alias keys; (c) re-evaluate kernel selector thresholds with simulated small-frag workload.
devon: logging idea: emit a metric when fragment_router switches to slowpath with contextual tags (header_flags, seq_len) so we can alert before tail shifts.
maria: good call — add it. i'll iterate on repro and bench results and post numbers here. :thumbsup:
